newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria sells electronics firm stake for $704,870.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria sells electronics firm stake for $704,870.

text.p: Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said on Tuesday it had sold 80 percent of bankrupt electronic components maker Mikroelektronika to Sofia-registered SecuryMark for $704,870.
Half of the price is to be paid in cash and the rest either in Brady bonds or in domestic bad debt bonds, a Privatisation Agency statement said.

The buyer has pledged to repay all the company's debts totalling some $7 million, to invest $11 million over the next five years and to increase current 400 job positions to 1,000 by the end of the period.
The remaining 20 percent equity would be offered at preferential prices to company employees.
Botevgrad-based Mikroelektronika produces electronics components and assembly units. Some 37 percent of its production was exported in 1995.
SecuryMark deals in marking cars and valuable objects against theft and forgery.

Mikroelektronika was declared bankrupt as of October 17, 1996. It was put on a list of 64 state firms earmarked for closure under a funding agreement with the International Monetary Fund sealed in July. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
